title: You don't own the company. You own a slice.
subject: stock market shares
hooks: You don't own the company. You own a slice.
Stop watching the chart. Start watching the business.
caption:
Stop staring at the chart. Start understanding the business. 📉📈 What's your biggest investing fear?

beats.text: You don't own the company. You own a slice.
A stock market is just a place to buy those slices.

props.prompt: busy stock trading floor with multiple monitors showing green charts, cinematic lighting, depth of field

beats.text: These slices are officially called shares.
When the company grows and earns more, your slice gets pricier.
Panic makes prices fall quickly, not necessarily instantly.
Daily price moves are chaotic noise for many investors.
Long-term investors usually focus on strong businesses instead.

props.prompt: calm person looking at laptop screen, ignoring red background screens, soft lighting, focus on face

beats.text: They focus only on strong underlying businesses.
Long-term focus on strong businesses is the usual strategy.

props.fact: Long-term focus on strong businesses is the usual strategy.
